newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-QBE says expects more profit growth.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-QBE says expects more profit growth.

text.p: QBE Insurance Ltd said on Monday it expected further profit growth in the 1996/97 year ending June 30.

"In the absence of unusual frequency or severity of claims, or a decline in investment markets, the directors are expecting further profit growth in the 1996/97 financial year," managing director John Cloney said in a statement.
Earlier, the company reported a year net profit of A$147.3 million, up from A$82.5 million previously.

Cloney said QBE continued to expand its businesses beyond Australia with around 60 percent of its premium income from primary and reinsurance activities currently stemming from its international operations.
He said the company expected to continue increasing its dividends in 1996/97.

International general insurance operations were expected to achieve overall growth in 1996/97, while the Australian general insurance operation was tipped to grow its premiums and maintain its profits.
Cloney said QBE's investment income was likely to improve due to higher fixed interest earnings combined with capital growth from equity investments and cashflow.
He attributed the improved 1995/96 result to an overall underwriting profit and an strong investment performance.
"We achieved solid premium growth despite the adverse effect of the strengthening Australian dollar and the Sequoia (Insurance Co) sale," Cloney said.
Gross earned premiums rose 9.8 percent to A$1.50 billion as a result of growth in Australian and international operations, while net earned premium income lifted 9.2 percent to A$1.13 billion.
Insurance profit, including investment income on insurance funds, climbed to A$89.8 million from A$79.2 million previously, and investment income increased 16.8 percent to A$149.7 million.
"Cash flow from operations, despite the appreciation of the Australian dollar, continues to be strong at A$190.2 million, compared to A$235.0 million last year," Cloney said.
Return on average funds employed was at 17.2 percent, up from 17.0 last year.
At 12.40 p.m. (0240 GMT), QBE shares were 24 cents firmer at A$7.84.
